issues.description: Constructors for Seal, Pig, and Goat: the commented example in the template src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java shows two-argument constructor calls (e.g. Seal("Clarabelle", "marine"), Pig("Doodle", "domestic"), Goat("Buttinsky", "mountain")), while the exercise UML and problem statement define Animal with a single attribute 'name' and the provided solution (and its Main.java) use single-argument constructors (e.g. Seal("Clarabelle")). This inconsistency between the template comment and the UML/solution can mislead students about the expected constructor parameter list and cause confusion when implementing or testing the classes.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor usage consistent across artifacts. Preferred fix: update the commented example in template src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java to use single-argument constructors that accept only the animal name (e.g. Seal("Clarabelle"), Pig("Doodle"), Goat("Buttinsky")) to match the UML/problem statement and the solution. Alternative: if an additional attribute is intended, update the UML/problem statement to list that attribute and update the solution and template constructors and examples to accept two parameters.
